# Biology-Genetics-9

## Background

The supplied data represent ten target haplotypes across 100 markers. The targets have equal weight. Target, state, marker and panel indices are zero-based.

A state index identifies the same composite trajectory along a target chromosome. At each marker, the panel digit identifies the reference panel supplying that state's allele. A mismatch digit of 0 denotes agreement with the target allele; a digit of 1 denotes disagreement.

The traces are the fixed inputs for this bounded composite-state experiment. No raw genotypes, genetic-map interpolation, state selection, target sampling or random chromosome simulation is required.

The full reference panels contain the following numbers of reference haplotypes. These counts describe the full panels.

| Reference panel | Reference haplotypes |
| --------------- | -------------------: |
| R0              |                  310 |
| R1              |                  270 |
| R2              |                  240 |
| R3              |                  180 |

Genetic coordinates are in centiMorgans (cM). Marker m is at the decimal coordinate 0.05 × m, for m = 0, …, 99.

| Experimental control                        |  Value |
| ------------------------------------------- | -----: |
| Ancestry-agnostic effective population size | 100000 |
| Local-record width                          | 0.5 cM |
| Minimum marker count per local record       |      9 |

Preserve the released implementation's window-membership, interval-to-window and record-selection conventions. The scientific algorithm snapshot is `ec0ad295aeebfacf10d8cbfb6486ab78981de1b1`.

**Numerical conventions**

* Use IEEE-754 binary64 for all calculations.
* Before clustering, round the reported local panel-probability coordinates to three decimal places, using nearest rounding with ties to even.
* Retain binary64 precision for local switch-rate records.
* At marker 0, the incoming-interval switching increment is zero.
* These precision and chromosome-start conventions replace the implementation's binary32 intermediates and initial interval record.
* Rates carried into the ancestry model are per Morgan; the genetic map remains in cM.
* Mathematical implementations with equivalent posterior probabilities are acceptable.

**Finite mixture controls**

The schedule below replaces the released program's stochastic initialization and stopping defaults. Each row is one start, in start-index order. The entries identify initial center records for the stated candidate K. Record indices follow window-major, target-minor order among the retained records.

| Start | K = 2  | K = 3      | K = 4          |
| ----: | ------ | ---------- | -------------- |
|     0 | 17, 38 | 99, 20, 70 | 66, 46, 75, 23 |
|     1 | 24, 52 | 7, 63, 87  | 34, 8, 66, 32  |
|     2 | 22, 64 | 68, 74, 54 | 25, 8, 49, 11  |
|     3 | 97, 2  | 26, 11, 35 | 23, 22, 71, 38 |
|     4 | 52, 83 | 87, 69, 89 | 79, 7, 29, 11  |
|     5 | 34, 58 | 87, 90, 95 | 14, 47, 32, 19 |
|     6 | 94, 85 | 99, 60, 13 | 92, 35, 79, 10 |
|     7 | 74, 7  | 79, 53, 82 | 88, 75, 53, 41 |
|     8 | 4, 13  | 32, 43, 96 | 96, 29, 76, 94 |
|     9 | 57, 48 | 76, 17, 91 | 32, 9, 73, 28  |

Each start uses its indicated records as the initial means, equal component weights and a common initial full covariance. This covariance is the maximum-likelihood covariance of the fitted coordinates plus 1e-6 times the identity matrix.

* Perform exactly 80 E-then-M cycles, using full covariance matrices.
* Add a fresh 1e-6 diagonal regularizer in every M step.
* Evaluate likelihoods and responsibilities after the final M step.
* Final total log likelihoods within 1e-9 of the largest are tied. Select the tied start with the lowest start index.
* Exact component-posterior ties select the lowest component index.
* A numerical component with effective mass at most 1e-12 is invalid. The supplied instance has no such component.

**Ancestry labels and experimental scope**

Assign ancestry labels once, after selecting K. Sort the complete initial copying-matrix rows lexicographically in reference-panel order R0, R1, R2, R3 and label them A0, A1, … . Exact row ties retain the selected fit's component order. Keep these identities during and after recalibration.

P[Ai,Rj] denotes the conditional copying probability for reference panel Rj in ancestry Ai.

The continuity threshold, largest-admissible-K policy, single conditional matrix update, posterior-fraction endpoint, label convention and finite mixture schedule are task-defined experimental controls. A candidate with an undefined continuity diagnostic is inadmissible. No second update, parameter re-estimation or ancestry relabeling is part of this experiment.

**Raw state traces**

Each row below gives one composite state for the indicated target. Both traces run from marker 0 through marker 99.

Each trace is displayed as five consecutive groups of 20 digits. In order, the groups cover markers 0–19, 20–39, 40–59, 60–79 and 80–99. Concatenate the five groups from left to right to recover the original trace. Spaces and visual line breaks are formatting only; retain all leading zeros.

## Problem

Admixed target haplotypes are represented by chromosome-wide composite-reference traces, with reference panels that may imperfectly represent the contributing ancestries. Identify the recent genetics treatment that learns ancestry representations from local reference-panel copying profiles and supports recalibration of ancestry-specific copying probabilities. In the supplied controlled experiment, an ancestry count is admissible when the treatment's minimum lag-one clustering-continuity diagnostic is finite and at least 0.10; use the largest admissible count among 2, 3 and 4. Determine the posterior mean fraction assigned to ancestry A0 after exactly one source-defined copying-matrix update, with the other model parameters held at their source-derived initial-model values, followed by inference under the updated matrix. The requested fraction refers to a uniformly sampled target-haplotype/marker pair in the supplied chromosome, and A0 follows the fixed label convention below.
In the reasoning, identify the source and justify the state construction, continuity decision, rate estimation and recalibration. Report the retained-window count, omitted panel coordinate, each candidate's minimum continuity diagnostic, selected ancestry count, all selected-model initial ancestry rates, initial P[A0,R3], pre-update posterior fraction for A0, updated P[A0,R0], P[A1,R3] and, if A2 exists, P[A2,R2]. Report final posterior checkpoints for A0 at target 7 / marker 47, A1 at target 4 / marker 12 and, if A2 exists, A2 at target 7 / marker 6; use these checkpoints to support the single final fraction. Give every reported non-integer value, including the final fraction, to at least eight decimal places.
